A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIM-PP research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison, including the image-based dataset analyses added in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and finetuned FIM-PP results on five real-world datasets, synthetic intensity estimates and prediction case studies, alongside externally sourced baseline results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds alternative-loss experiments, initialization comparisons, context-size sensitivity tests and synthetic-process evaluations.

M1.justification: v2 introduces an evaluated supervised sMAPE training variant in Section 4.2 and Tables 3–5. The primary NLL-trained architecture, intensity parameterization, normalization and inference procedure remain unchanged. The broader description of process families does not establish a changed pretraining generator: the corresponding configuration tables are identical.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on an unseen power-law interaction kernel, explicitly excluded from pretraining (Appendix A.1, Figure 4). The five real-world datasets and synthetic training families remain unchanged. Gamma, Poisson and Rayleigh processes highlighted in the new evaluation figure were already represented in v1's training coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds randomly initialized FIM-PP as a comparator for pretrained initialization in Figure 5, and sMAPE-trained variants alongside NLL-trained models in Tables 3–5. The external comparator sets in the corresponding multi-event and next-event benchmark comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols compare initialization through validation-NLL trajectories and vary context size from 100 to 2000 paths, using 100 points per path and intensity sMAPE (Figures 5–6). Existing benchmark splits, metrics and documented training settings remain unchanged. Section 5.2 also changes test sequences from providing 'history' to providing 'context', conflicting with Appendix E; an actual change in test-data use is unconfirmed.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis through pretraining-versus-random-initialization controls, context-size sensitivity, alternative-loss comparisons, synthetic intensity-recovery examples including distribution shift, and synthetic-versus-real dataset statistics (Figures 4–12 and Tables 3–5). The original Taxi failure and adaptation case studies are retained as Figures 13–14.

E5.justification: Benchmark tables retain mean and standard deviation over 10 trials, including the added sMAPE rows. However, new Figure 6 displays error bars without identifying their statistic or repetition count. Whether this introduces a different uncertainty-estimation practice cannot be reliably determined.

E6.justification: All retained benchmark scores are unchanged after matching v1's FIM-PP rows to v2's NLL rows. v2 adds sMAPE-variant results across five datasets and three horizons, including finetuned Taxi OTD of 16.493 ± 0.034 at N=20. New intensity-recovery, convergence, context-sensitivity and dataset-statistics findings substantially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, intensity equations, normalization derivation, NLL expressions and evaluation-metric formulas are retained. v2's explanations of scalability and expressive capacity add no formal result, proof or revised derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed match to specialized models from next-event prediction to multi-event prediction. The central contributions—synthetic pretraining, in-context intensity inference, zero-shot transfer and rapid finetuning—remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting hierarchical encoding to scalability and history-dependent parameters to richer intensity behavior. It interprets the new analyses as supporting broad prior coverage and robustness to larger contexts, and motivates NLL over supervised sMAPE through computational cost and flexibility. Existing Taxi/Taobao failure explanations and principal applicability limits remain.

D1.justification: The abstract and Section 7 change reported model, repository and tutorial availability from forthcoming to available. v2 adds a baseline-code access reference, finetuning requirements of a few minutes and at most 11 GB, and Figure 5's definition of an epoch as one inference-path prediction. Existing architecture and pretraining details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu and Quan's TPP-LLM and distinguishes its finetuning requirement from FIM-PP's zero-shot operation. It also adds Draxler et al., Hu et al. and two Mauel works. The broader research positioning remains stable; publication metadata updates to existing references are not new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, introduction and conclusion, reorganizes Section 4.1 into an explicit process-family list, and expands Section 5.2 with topical paragraphs. Additional Results moves from Appendix F to Appendix A with subsections. The main section sequence and most technical appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds nine figures covering synthetic predictions, convergence, context sensitivity and six dataset-statistics displays (Figures 4–12). The long-horizon tables gain loss-labeled variant rows, and the generation tables move to the end. Original Figures 1–3 and the Taxi examples are retained, with the latter renumbered 13–14.

improvement.justification: The initialization controls, context-size tests and additional synthetic evaluations make the benefits and boundaries of pretraining more directly assessable. The abstract's multi-event claim better matches the retained benchmark evidence, and reported resource availability improves reproducibility information. These gains are limited by undefined Figure 6 error bars, sparse alternative-loss documentation and conflicting test-context descriptions in Section 5.2 and Appendix E.
